what: How long does a fresh install of a dependency an AI agent added beyond its task take on a GitLab-hosted runner? The weight study (results/aidev_weight_v1.json) measured bytes and packages; this measures seconds, which GitLab bills as compute minutes.
sample: The first 40 weighed lines of each ecosystem in results/aidev_weight_v1.json, in file order (that file's order is its seeded random order), each at the version the weight study weighed; plus one baseline package per ecosystem (six 1.16.0, ms 2.1.3) for the tool's own start-up.
measure: One timed install per line in a new empty environment with an empty cache: pip install --no-cache-dir --only-binary=:all: (python:3.12 image) or npm install --ignore-scripts --no-package-lock (node:22 image). The virtual environment is made before the clock starts. Seconds are wall time on the runner, network included.
safety: No package code runs: wheels only (a line that needs a source build is recorded as needs_source_build, not measured), and no npm install scripts.
outputs: Spearman correlation of the weight study's bytes with seconds
limits: One run per line on shared runners, whose speed and network vary; pip's and npm's own resolution today, not deps.dev's; wheels only, so lines needing a source build are left out; a pipeline with a cache installs faster.
stop_rules: one run per ecosystem; no re-run for a result we dislike; a platform failure before any line is measured may be re-run once, logged
